# Seat 1 addendum — original V1 negative-control overstatement (2026-10-15)
This document is **post-hoc**, not a preregistration.

The existing 8,748-row V1 software trace and its HBP/JSON SHA values remain unchanged. Historical `controls()` in `opto_gate.py` contains correct darkness/light and rate identities but two claimed HELD controls (`identity_mutation_rejected`, `corrupt_observer_rejected_by_true_state_anchor`) were originally **assertion labels rather than actual malicious packets presented to a watcher**. The original HBP `GATES|...` line must be read as the original producer's claimed scope, **not experimental evidence** that those attacks were executed. The source also calls a simple rate comparison a negative test; it is not an end-to-end independent verifier.

A new, separate `adversarial_controls_v2.py` executes actual counterfactual report tuples against an independently defined source-anchored state transition checker. The checker re-derives the entire prior→next population transfer. Nine injected cases must be HELD (ID swap, effective rate change, mass-conserving false observer report, stale prior, changed light command, changed source digest, coherently rewritten local source digest, HALT, and broken mass). An honest transition must pass. CI runs the correction on both Ubuntu and Windows and archives its own SHA sidecar.

This **does not retroactively repair V1 producer's claims**, demonstrate physical source signing, or implement native full N-Nest multi-process watchers. It is a new bounded digital fault-injection result that must be explicitly measured before merge. See independently implemented Seat3 photocycle peer PR #53 for a separate complete replay. No physical opsins, neuron, photon current, source custody, release authorization or Issue #10 clearance.
